headline: Evidence is the basis for knowledge—what we see, measure, and verify about reality
universal_truth: Claims without evidence are opinions; the strength of your belief should match the strength of your evidence
fun_facts: Scientists require evidence to be reproducible—others must be able to get the same results
Anecdotes are the weakest form of evidence—one case doesn't prove a pattern
Confirmation bias leads us to notice evidence for what we already believe and ignore evidence against
discussion_questions: How do you evaluate evidence for claims you hear?
What do you believe without good evidence?
How do you distinguish between strong and weak evidence?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Anyone can claim anything. What separates knowledge from belief? Evidence. Observations, measurements, experiments—things we can verify, test, and replicate. Evidence is how we know what's actually true.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We're flooded with claims—in news, online, from friends. How do we know what to believe?

options.text: Claims should be proportional to evidence—extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence; the strength of belief should match the quality and quantity of supporting evidence
options.response: Yes. A claim that it will rain tomorrow needs modest evidence. A claim that aliens visited needs extraordinary evidence. Match confidence to evidence quality.
Reliable sources help, but the best approach is understanding their evidence, not just their reputation...

q1.title: Evidence Hierarchy
q1.script: Not all evidence is equal. Anecdotes are weak. Case studies are better. Controlled experiments are better still. Replicated, peer-reviewed studies are strongest. Know the hierarchy.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Evidence Hierarchy"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Confirmation Bias
q2.script: We naturally notice evidence for what we believe and dismiss evidence against. Fighting this bias requires actively seeking disconfirming evidence, not just confirming.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Proportional Belief
q3.script: Strong evidence warrants strong belief. Weak evidence warrants tentative belief. No evidence warrants no belief. Calibrate your confidence to your evidence.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Claims without evidence are opinions. The strength of your belief should match the strength of your evidence. Demand evidence.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 294. Tomorrow, we'll explore guesses you can test—hypotheses. Until then, examine the evidence for something you believe.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Evidence Audit - What Do You Really Know?
growTrack.learning_objective: Evaluate the evidence basis for current beliefs
growTrack.activity: Pick a belief you hold strongly. What's the evidence for it? What's the evidence against it? Have you sought disconfirming evidence? Is your confidence calibrated to your evidence?
